detail: Notes 1 and 2, the far-bank strata and grass (CreekBack, shared by creek-wide and car-swept). The four full-width ruled bands are gone. Each of the four courses (rows about bankY-96+22c) is now a run of separate blocks:
- blocks 70 to 150 units long, each drawn as a 9-point polygon whose top is jittered about ±2.5 units;
- each block's own row moves up or down by up to about 6 units, so neighbouring blocks step;
- each block is 19 to 28 units thick;
- 14 percent of blocks are skipped, and the dark limestoneDeep backing shows through the gap;
- 25 percent of joints open 6 to 22 units;
- 10 percent of blocks in the upper courses are slumped, tilted up to ±3.5 degrees and dropped 4 units;
- clusters of brush ellipses fall every 110 units over the joints, and cracks are short and angled.

No block edge is longer than 150 units. The grass is one closed smooth path, with points every 38 units on both its top and its lower edge. Each edge combines three sine waves with random jitter, of ±6 on the top and ±7 (plus an occasional +8 droop) on the lower edge. Tufts hang below the lower edge. The closing verticals at x -360 and 1560 are off frame in both cameras.

Notes 3 to 5, the water's far edge and the pale band. The s3 sheet footprint now follows creekToe sampled every 24 units through a smooth path. creekToe is 1086 plus three sines (amplitudes 7, 4 and 2.5; periods about 483, 134 and 48) plus a 13-unit Gaussian bulge round each of the 5 slumped blocks. Across the visible span (world x of about 0 to 916 in car-swept), that gives about 14 units of peak-to-peak swing every 240 units plus the bulges, so the edge is not a near-collinear run. ext.y0 is now bankY-20, and lit is .002, so the pale SA.waterLit top colour reaches SA.water by about y 1074. That is above the lowest point of the toe, so no pale band remains along the top of the water. The lowest course and the backing end at toe+16 and toe+24, under the water. CreekToe adds the following on the sheet: overlapping shadow pools of uneven depth, oak shadows, scattered short pale reflections, slumped blocks with foam collars and shed eddies, and foam in pieces every 90 units.

Note 6, the landmark ledge (CreekLedge). Its waterline is a 13-point wandering line with a 9-unit dip where a block has slumped from its middle. The straight 210-unit bottom is gone. The undercut band runs over 9 jittered points, its top is hand-stepped and its foam is broken into 4 pieces. The ledge's position is unchanged at [90, 250].

Note 6, the near bank (CreekBank). Each course's top and bottom are now zigzag polylines with points every 55 units. The white water on the bank face is in 3 broken strokes, and two more brush clumps were added.

Note 6, the swell hairline (CreekShelf). The shelf fill is now opaque #977E58 (about the old .7 tint over this water). The back layer is drawn whole. The front layer is clipped 1.5 units above the FloodSheet's swell, so the two overlap with no antialiased seam. At row 1170 the mask is fully opaque, so drawing twice leaves no mark. The far and near sides now have 14 wandering points each. The back layer's clip rectangle (x -700..1900, y 724..1720) lies outside the mask's nonzero rows, so it draws no edge.
- s4: no lit prop, so the gradient keeps the tone's own midAt; ext and floodFoot as before. Other FloodSheet users receive no lit.
- CREEK, CREEK_MARKS, CREEK_CAR, CREEK_CAM, S3, s3Off, s3Car, CREEK_PLAN and the creek-plan case are as in rounds 19 and 23.
- With width [-300, 1500], CREEK_OAKS still places the landmark oak at x 420, base 992.
- The layer order is the same, with CreekToe added between the back sheet and CreekLedge.

- All rows that changed lie between world y of about 976 and 1130, which is about 924 to 1078 on screen in creek-wide and about 850 to 1031 in car-swept. That is well above the caption band. The near bank's rows are unchanged.

story_review.one_viewing_summary: Intended chain, read from code and not observed:
one_viewing_summary_detail: A generic white driverless car brakes into an airport bay while its empty wheel turns, and the phone says Arriving.
A map outlines the limited February area of 60 square miles.
A different empty car stands at a creek's shallow edge in rain, under a broken limestone bank with live oaks. The current shoves it off the stone lip and carries it past a fixed oak and ledge.
Another empty car stops in rising street floodwater with its hazards blinking.
A recall card shows Software and 3,791, the icon grid fills and a stamp lands.
A car slows and then rolls into standing water while 'may' lights.
The remedy row is stamped Under development.
In a wet lot a weather limits tag clips above four cars. In a low close each car takes its check and an April 20 page flips.
The curb returns with the door open beside the remedy card.
story_review.opening_to_ending: The opening question asks what the federal record says about the flood problem now that the airport ride is open. The close answers it: the open curb door beside 'The remedy is currently under development'. No repair or outcome is invented.
story_review.weakest_transition: s2 to s3 at 12.36 s. The map cuts to the creek with no carried subject; the handoff relies on 'In April' and the disclosure.
